purpose.content: Aster is a fictional greenhouse sensor hub. The requirements cover periodic sampling and export of one temperature reading while leaving actuator control outside the product boundary.

fields.system_boundary: The Aster hub samples its local probe and exports readings; greenhouse actuators and weather prediction are external.

requirements.content: The hub shall sample every 60 seconds, timestamp each sample in UTC, and export a reading only after validation. Timely delivery matters because irrigation decisions consume the data.

fields.normative_statements: Sample at 60-second intervals, record UTC timestamps, reject non-finite values, and preserve the latest valid reading during export outages.
fields.rationale: Predictable cadence and validated timestamps let the external controller compare independent sensor hubs without accepting corrupt readings.

acceptance.content: Acceptance uses a fictional ten-minute run with a controllable clock and one injected invalid sample; these are planned criteria, not an executed test result.

fields.measurable_conditions: Ten valid samples arrive at 60±0.1-second intervals, invalid input is rejected, and the last valid reading remains available throughout a two-minute outage.
fields.verification_method: Demonstrate sampling and outage behavior with a fake clock, scripted probe inputs, and an export recorder.

trace.content: Example::Sensor and Example::Controller identify the model participants for the sampling requirement and its intended sampling design.

fields.model_elements: Example::Sensor and Example::Controller provide the fictional source elements for the sampling requirement.
fields.design_links: The Aster reading-pipeline design owns validation and export behavior; no implementation result is asserted here.

limits.content: Probe accuracy, hardware timing jitter, and security deployment settings are not specified by this small fictional requirements example.

fields.unresolved_items: Probe calibration limits, real scheduler jitter, authentication, and production retention remain for the actual project to decide.
